tier: historical hosted CI service (end of life)
confidence_note: The end-of-life notice and the API documentation are first-party CloudBees pages captured and quoted. No build was run and no account was opened. No first-party page read states a recurring free allowance for private projects, so the historical free tier is unverified from a first-party source.

free_tier.stated: unverified: no first-party page read states a standing free allowance for private projects. The last published first-party price list starts at USD 49 per month (CodeShip Basic Starter). A former free tier for public open-source projects is described by third parties only and is not established here
free_tier.notes: The preserved pricing page lists paid tiers of USD 49, USD 99 and USD 399 per month. The unit is none because no standing free allowance is established; a paid-only tier is not a free tier. A USD price is quoted with its ISO 4217 code.

per_object_cap.stated: unverified: no per-object cap is stated on the pages read; the service ran builds rather than storing objects

retention.stated: unverified: no build or build-log retention period is stated on the pages read

egress.terms: unverified: no egress allowance or per-gigabyte price is stated on the pages read. The preserved pricing page describes build concurrency and parallel test pipelines, not network egress

interface_detail: A REST API v2 under api.codeship.com let a client list projects, trigger builds and inspect pipelines. Access to the API used a token obtained by Basic Auth from the authentication endpoint; the API is documented as part of the now unsupported product.
tooling: A hosted CI service reached through a web console, a connected source-control repository and the REST API. A project member with a password account invoked the API with a bearer token; no client binary was supplied by the pages read.
chaining: A push to a connected repository started a build; the API could trigger and inspect builds. The service reached end of life and CloudBees directs users to migrate to CloudBees Unify, so this chain no longer runs on Codeship.

limits.value: As of January 2026, CloudBees no longer supports the CloudBees CodeShip product, so no new build can be started
historical paid tiers named 1, 2 or 4 concurrent builds and 2 or 4 parallel test pipelines

limits_note: Concurrency figures come from the preserved paid price list and describe the retired paid tiers, not a live allowance.
binding_note: The end-of-life notice stops new builds for every tier, so product discontinuation binds before any historical concurrency figure.

identity_cost.detail: A password account on CodeShip was required; a GitHub, GitLab or Bitbucket account alone would not work for API users, and accounts with two-factor authentication would not work. New users were invited by email address. No sign-up was performed and no card or phone requirement is established from the page read

reliability_note: The hosted product reached end of life; CloudBees states that it no longer supports CodeShip and recommends migration to CloudBees Unify.

evidence.quote: As of January 2026, CloudBees no longer supports the CloudBees CodeShip product.
evidence.proved: the CodeShip product reached end of life and is unsupported

evidence.quote: CloudBees recommends migrating to CloudBees Unify, which provides a modern, scalable, and secure CI/CD platform with enhanced features and capabilities. For more information about CloudBees Unify and how it can benefit your organization, please visit the [CloudBees Unify product page](https://www.cloudbees.com/unify).
evidence.proved: the vendor directs users to migrate to CloudBees Unify

evidence.quote: Users that want to access the API also need to have a password account on CodeShip, so regular GitHub/GitLab/Bitbucket accounts will not work.
evidence.proved: a password account was required for API access; social login alone was not sufficient

evidence.quote: To create a new user, simply invite them using an appropriate email address.
evidence.proved: new API users were invited by email address

evidence.quote: The authentication endpoint uses [Basic Auth](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Authentication#basic_authentication_scheme) to authenticate the user and return an auth token.
evidence.proved: API access used a token obtained through Basic Auth

notes: A hosted CI service that was discontinued. Both CodeShip Basic and CodeShip Pro ran on the CloudBees platform and are covered by one end-of-life notice, so one record holds the provider. A later successor, CloudBees Unify, is a distinct offer with no first-party free allowance established here.
